topics.topic: Ownership of A7 rule 3 settling decision and marked_at assignment
questions: Does `system_clock` own all of A7 rule 3, including deciding settling status and setting `marked_at`, or only producing a current time in the required form; if only the latter, which modules own those other clauses?
Does `system_clock` own all of A7 rule 3, including deciding settling status and setting `marked_at`, or only the clock reading and its form; if only part, which modules own the remaining clauses?

Who owns the parts of A7 rule 3 that use the reading to decide settling status and set `marked_at`, since `system_clock` must not own comparisons and the state otherwise assigns those behaviors to `source_folder` and `photo_delivery`?

quotes: | A7 | rules 1 and 3, the clock and the form of its reading | `system_clock` |
- ignored names, links, the settling time, source limits and file signatures;
- one mark per placement, replay and `publication_conflict`;
judgement.why: The ownership row limits system_clock to the clock and its form, while source_folder owns the settling decision and photo_delivery owns creation of the mark that contains marked_at.

topics.topic: Operation-scoped value carrying the single connections-file snapshot
questions: What operation-scoped value carries the single judged file reading from `confirmed_connection` to `available_photo_folder`, and which module owns that value and its lifetime?

How is the single connections-file reading carried from `confirmed_connection` to `available_photo_folder` so that the latter cannot reread the file and the operation continues on the original snapshot?

quotes:
The operations
read the record themselves through `confirmed_connection`, so no module keeps connections in memory.

### Candidate public capabilities

```text
load_connections
confirmed_connection
available_photo_folder
```
judgement.why: This is the same question already judged in P19 about the exact inputs, outputs and lifetime parameters of the object_connections capabilities, and the relevant passages have not changed.

topics.topic: Wording of photo_delivery clock injection without naming utc_now
questions: Rewrite the passage so the description of `photo_delivery` refers to the injected clock callable without naming the foreign export `utc_now` as a whole word.

Rewrite the passage so the note explains callable injection without naming the foreign export `utc_now` as something `photo_delivery` calls, while retaining the declared `deliverer_api` → `system_clock` dependency.

quotes:
`system_clock` is the module that `system_clock_backend` generates. `deliverer_api` alone names it, and
hands `utc_now` to an operation as a function that `photo_delivery` calls.
judgement.why: The note names the foreign export `utc_now` as a whole word in connection with photo_delivery even though the declared dependency belongs only to deliverer_api.
